dedupe_keys.name: osmre national mine map repository nmmr

description: A national archive of maps of closed and abandoned mines in the United States. The OSMRE page says the repository holds maps of more than 275,000 closed or abandoned mines from the 1790s to the present, indexed with more than 40 fields per map, that users can search and view the maps online through a web map application and request images, and that it goes back to the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Act of 1969. Searching and viewing are free; image requests go to the repository. Coverage is the United States, for coal and non-coal mines. Caveats: the page read does not give a licence or a bulk download, and old maps can be incomplete or inaccurate about the true extent of workings. For simulation it shows where underground workings lie beneath roads, rail, pipelines and buildings, to assess subsidence and mine flooding risks for planned or existing infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the OSMRE e-AMLIS inventory.
